summary: Reed never persists a per-session geometry field; the only stored size is Config.Width/Height, used solely as the boot-time new-session -x/-y and as liveBoxLocked's fallback. The operator's terminal size is read once, at attach time, via golang.org/x/term.GetSize in reedcli's attachCmd, and handed to Engine.AttachArgv, which computes a window_layout string against that told box and chains a select-layout onto the attach-session argv so it applies the instant tmux (via the pinned window-size=latest option) has already resized the real window to the client -- this ordering is the reconciliation: AttachArgv deliberately never queries the live (still pre-attach, stale) window, trusting the freshly-read told size instead, and the two effective-value readbacks (window-size, status) reconcile reed's intended pins against what tmux actually honored, suppressing the chained layout on disagreement. Re-attaching runs the identical path with no special-casing. A terminal resizing while already attached (no new attach) is handled entirely by tmux itself via the window-size=latest pin -- reed has no resize command, hook, or SIGWINCH handling anywhere in reedengine or reedcli. Every other mutating op (Up/Resume/Add/Remove/UpdateStrand) instead re-queries the live window fresh via liveBoxLocked on each call, because a stale/mismatched layout string gets silently rescaled by tmux rather than rejected.
